newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Kucan gives Drnovsek mandate to rule.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Kucan gives Drnovsek mandate to rule.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Monday gave acting premier Janez Drnovsek a mandate to form the next government and urged party leaders to break a political deadlock following inconclusive general elections.
"I name Janez Drnovsek as candidate for prime minister... He is the leader of the party that won most votes in the election," Kucan told a news conference.
Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats emerged as the strongest party in the November 10 general election, winning 25 of 90 parliamentary seats.
But Drnovsek is faced with an alliance of three right-wing parties who together won 45 seats in the former Yugoslav republic's second general election since independence in 1991.
With one seat short of an absolute majority, the alliance headed by conservative People's Party leader Marjan Podobnik, appeared reluctant to give up the fight to form the next administration.
Kucan said nearly two months of talks with leaders of the political parties showed that the right-wing and centre-left blocs were becoming entrenched, with neither side willing to back the other.
"I am surprised by the firm stand being taken by the political parties which is getting even firmer," Kucan said.

Drnovsek, 46, needs to win over at least one of the rightwing parties to break the deadlock, even if he wins support from smaller parties, such as the United List of Social Democrats, the former communists.
Drnovsek, speaking after Kucan's announcement, acknowledged that forming the next government was not going to be easy.
"I have accepted the candidacy...The possibilities of gaining an absolute majority are realistic, although the vote in parliament is uncertain," he told reporters.
Kucan said he would lodge Drnovsek's nomination with parliament on Friday. Deputies then have seven days to vote on whether to back or reject Drnovsek's candidacy.
"In the talks to come, I will try to increase my support (in parliament)...The task is relatively hard," Drnovsek said.
